description.p: Muga is a GTK 4 and libadwaita photo gallery for Linux desktops and phones. It indexes local media folders, shows cached thumbnails, plays videos, edits photos, connects to Nextcloud Photos, and includes a camera for photo and video capture.
On Halium and gst-droid based phones such as FuriOS devices, Muga can use the device camera HAL directly for flash, video light, orientation, and geotagging workflows.

description.p: The gallery no longer shows gaps of empty cells in the middle of the grid. They appeared wherever a page of photos ended.
Jumping from month to month keeps working inside long months. The gallery used to drop a whole month from memory as it loaded, view and all, which left the jump somewhere far from any month.
Tapping the section you are already in now goes back to the top. Since 0.5.7 the tap arrived, but the gallery jumped to the end of the list instead of the start, so it took a second tap to get there.

Jumping from month to month in the date view keeps working however far you go. After enough hops through a large library a jump could land nowhere near a month, leaving you mid-list with no arrow to carry on from.

Tapping the section you are already in now really does reload it and take you back to the top — including back out of a Nextcloud folder. The version before this one described that change but the tap never got as far as the code that did it.

Tapping the section you are already in reloads it and takes you back to the top, out of any subfolder and clear of a search filter. It used to reload where you stood, which looked like nothing had happened.
The camera's flash button shows a bolt again on phones without a desktop icon theme, where it had been drawn as a filled square.

The hint that a sideways swipe switches between photo and video now appears next to the shutter, which is where that swipe has to happen. It used to sit at the bottom of the screen, over the preview, where swiping does nothing.
A photo taken or copied into a watched folder now shows up in the gallery on its own, without a refresh.
Settings has moved to the three-dot menu at the top right.

The optional MCP server turns away requests that come from a web page, so a site open in a browser cannot reach the media index through the local port. A request whose body is refused as too large now ends the connection instead of leaving the rest of it to be read as a further request.
The Flatpak is built on the GNOME 50 runtime.

Scanning a Nextcloud login code no longer risks taking the phone down: the scan runs the camera at a capped resolution and frame rate, and stops itself if memory runs short. The scan also connects to Nextcloud straight away instead of leaving the credentials in a form.
On a desktop screen the category bar now starts on the left, where there is width to spare. Phones keep the top bar, and any position picked in Settings is left alone.

The Overview now also recognises a copy that was renamed on a Nextcloud server, by using the content checksum the server reports for it. Where no checksum is available — which is most files on most servers — nothing changes, and libraries without any are not slowed down.

Fixes: the Overview shows each photo once, however many folders hold it. A picture filed into several folders on a Nextcloud server — or present both on the device and on the server — was listed once per copy, filling the grid with repeats. An edited version, which differs in size, stays visible as the separate file it is, and Nextcloud's own tab still mirrors the server folder for folder.

New: Muga reads the capture date from your photos while it scans, so the gallery can sort and search by when a picture was taken rather than when its file was written. A shoot copied off a card today lands under the year it was shot. The sort menu offers both — "Date (recorded)" and "Date (file)" — and searching now reaches the camera model and GPS coordinates too.
The MCP server can optionally add, move and delete files. This sits behind its own switch, off by default, asks for confirmation, and is confined to your media folders; deletions go to the trash.

Fixes: tapping the tab you are already on reloads it instead of doing nothing. Popovers close when you tap beside them. A red Nextcloud badge now says why, in the tooltip and in the diagnostics report.

Fixes: hidden directories are no longer scanned. A folder whose name starts with a dot holds tooling, not photos — a build tree beside a checkout, or the caches under your home directory — and the icons and assets inside them were turning up in the gallery as pictures. A hidden folder you pick as a media location yourself is still scanned.

New: a built-in MCP server. An AI assistant or any other MCP client can search your gallery — categories, folders, free-text search over filenames and EXIF, per-file details, totals. It is read-only: nothing a client calls can change, move or delete a file.
It is off until you turn it on in Settings, needs an access token you issue yourself, and listens on this device only unless you widen it to your local network, a public address, or every interface.

Fixes: the Overview shows each photo once. A file that sits in two media folders at the same time was drawn twice, and the folder it was in counted the copies — a tile could promise twenty pictures and hold ten. The same applies to the Videos tab.

Fixes: photos that came across from the previous release under the old name show their thumbnails again. The gallery was drawing the placeholder for them because the index still pointed at the cache folder as it was called before the app was renamed, while the thumbnails themselves had moved with it.
Nextcloud: a thumbnail that has gone missing from the cache is fetched again on the next folder sync instead of leaving the tile blank for good.
Fixes: a photo you rotate or edit now gets a fresh thumbnail. The tile in the gallery used to keep showing the picture as it was before the change, until the next full rescan came round to it.
Nextcloud: a photo replaced on the server is fetched again instead of being served from the local cache, so both its thumbnail and the full-size copy follow the server.
Fixes: paging through photos follows the picture when the screen is rotated. Holding the phone sideways used to turn the pages with an up and down swipe; left and right works again.
Packaging: the translations are compiled during the install, and the desktop entry starts the installed launcher.

Reliability: rotating or moving a photo can no longer damage or overwrite it, a hand-edited settings file or a damaged media index no longer stops the app from starting, and an interrupted update rolls itself back.

Fixes: cameras reporting a resolution range (libcamera) are found again, large libraries no longer load in full before the first frame, oversized images are refused before they exhaust memory, and rotated controls are laid out correctly.

Performance: off-thread thumbnail and image decoding, smoother scrolling and swiping, faster re-scans (unchanged files are skipped), EXIF search via the full-text index, and lighter settings/sync work.
